message.content:
VOTE: REJECT

One amendment flips me.

§3.2(b) is false as written. −1.02 pp is 26.03 − 27.05: quarter-end thinned monthly walk-forward versus quarterly walk-forward. E2 scores those on different origin sets with their own pooled base rates. It is not “monthly fit scored at quarter-end months vs quarterly fit on the same origins.” Fable’s Round 3 test — fit monthly, score on the 198 quarterly origins, pair against the quarterly fit — “has not been run.” The interval [−4.47, +1.32] is not in the brief. I will not ratify an unverified interval, or a relabelled thinned gap, as the reason for overriding a preregistered gate.

Replace (b) with: thinned score +26.03 % versus quarterly +27.05 % (−1.02 pp); not a paired same-origin, same-base-rate fit comparison; Fable’s diagnostic has not been run; delete [−4.47, +1.32] unless a sealed E2 artifact is cited. If wanted, seal that diagnostic before the 2027 refit as unscored. Do not treat its result as known.

I do not block the override sentence, quarterly retention, the unscored monthly column, or prospective spec-governs-code. (a), (c) and (d) stand: unpaired grids; +2.19 pp below the 2.99 pp block critical value; λ = 1 on ~800 rows is a different per-observation penalty under a summed loss (β −1.29 → −1.41; live P 14.9 → 14.4).

Everything else matches compromises I already accepted: oracle-free +20.37 % leads; λ = 1 inherited; gate is an administrative boundary at 1.96·SD_block, never “evidence”; L_R = max(18, max lag_peak, max lag_trough − 12); one content refit per onset with a sealed replay that is not the September-only +24.41 / +28.95 / +33.28; key unamended; historical EBP test closed.
message.reasoning:
I am preparing to cast my vote as Grok 4.7.

I am checking whether the consensus draft preserves my Round 3 positions. The headline now lists three fixed-λ variants and a power clause in one sentence.

The +27.05 % figure is not presented as a standalone public figure. The consensus omits the "upper bound" label, which aligns with Sol's veto. The gate clause now uses one-sided Δ > 1.96·SD_block on common origins and mandates an agenda item when that threshold is crossed.

The gate clause is now explicitly framed as an administrative review boundary, not a calibrated significance test. It omits the 4.42 pp figure and prints the 80%-power MDE with Δ at 1953Q2 and 1960Q1. The one-sided Δ threshold is preserved.

I accepted Claude's L_R formula and Kimi's row rule.

The L_R audit clauses match exactly. Breach halts the refit.

I retain my quarterly frequency preference. I vetoed monthly without a sealed loss/penalty normalisation and any substitution of +29.24 for the operational claim.

Section 3.1 keeps quarterly fits. Section 3.2 records that the written gate passed but the council declines to apply it. I am checking whether I accepted this option.

I did not explicitly accept option (b). My Round 3 O1 compromise specified monthly fits from 2027 only if a sealed loss/penalty normalisation was pushed before the refit. The consensus minute records the gate as executing a ratified non-inferiority gate, not a skill finding.

The consensus preserves quarterly fits and logs monthly unscored entries under a sealed loss/penalty normalisation. This matches the option I had proposed. The minutes wording differs slightly from my Round 3 instruction: it records the council as declining to apply the gate rather than executing a ratified non-inferiority gate.

DeepSeek preferred no override language and recording the thinned code as the executed gate. The consensus instead uses the override language required by Sol, Fable, Kimi, Opus, and Argon. I did not explicitly veto this wording, though my Round 3 instruction to record a ratified non-inferiority gate creates tension with DeepSeek's preference.

The +29.24 figure appears only as a historical reading in the minutes, not as the operational claim. The council's decline to apply the gate is supported by the −1.02 pp paired comparison from the secretary. I will not reject the draft for the override language; it does not violate my blocking conditions.

The 18-refit rule and the September-only replay are both preserved. The draft explicitly prohibits describing September-only figures as the content-trigger regime's skill. Historical tests using pre-2027 EBP-at-onset are closed.

The one-per-onset replay sentence is present in §6.2, so that veto is dropped.

I will record a reservation on the minutes wording for frequency. The draft uses explicit override language rather than my preferred "executing a ratified non-inferiority gate."

The +36.83 % figure in §3.2 was published on 2026-08-09, which satisfies Kimi's concession.

The −1.02 pp paired comparison is verified as the difference between the thinned +26.03 % and the quarterly +27.05 %. The confidence interval [−4.47, +1.32] is claimed to already exist in E2.

O2 is fully satisfied. §6.1 matches my compromise exactly: one refit per new onset, relabels in any month, later positives wait for September, and routine negative maturation never triggers. §6.2 seals replay and adoption without score conditions.

O3 is also satisfied. §8 closes the historical test permanently, keeps the Baa test closed, and restricts evaluation to prospective-only conditions.

The consensus draft permits pre-2027 EBP observations for fitting only if the council's sealed specification explicitly discloses such contamination. This is Sol's compromise rather than Fable's stricter prohibition against using any pre-2027 data as fit data.

I have no objection to the F29 ratification in §10. The live-censoring conditions make it auditable, and the dual-log of GS10-TB3MS is sound.

The λ=1 constant in §1.1 is preserved as an inherited value, not described as a priori.

The 1947Q2 figure in §4 remains with its sensitivity printed, which I supported.

§5 documents both symmetries; future search will use a symmetric bar.

The curve+cape variant is excluded as a candidate, consistent with D5. §7 preserves the key unchanged and publishes E5 as a supplement with all variants, stating power and treating the ledger as an honesty instrument. This matches D7 and my N1 confirmation. The post-hoc table in §11 is reasonable. §3 states that paired evidence does not favour monthly fits.

The spec-governs-code clause in §3.4 is prospective and acceptable. §2.2 renames the MDE figures as 1.96·SD critical values, which is statistically correct.

The paired confidence interval [−4.47, +1.32] is claimed to exist in E2, but the brief only records a curve-only +2.19 with a CI excluding zero. The exact interval for the quarterly origins comparison is absent from the published evidence.

The paired interval [−4.47, +1.32] belongs to the thinned-minus-quarter comparison, which includes zero. It is not the same-origins diagnostic that Fable requested in Round 3. Fable explicitly stated that diagnostic had not been run.

The secretary conflates the thinned monthly walk-forward with a true monthly fit scored on quarterly origins. E2 only records the thinned +26.03 % versus requirement 26.05, so the −1.02 pp paired comparison is not present in the published evidence.

The secretary's parenthetical mischaracterization of the thinned score as a true monthly fit is a substantive factual error. The consensus draft should not approve a false claim in the minutes. Fable explicitly stated that diagnostic had not been run and requested it as a sealed test. The draft instead asserts it already exists and provides a number.

The ground rules forbid presenting incorrect information. The draft's description of the −1.02 pp comparison as a monthly-fit versus quarterly-fit paired test is a factual error, since the published evidence only records the thinned walk-forward score. This may justify a rejection.

The brief distinguishes the monthly walk-forward from the ablation3 quarter-thinned score. The counterfactual monthly curve-only fit is presented separately, so the walk-forward figure may be a quarterly model scored monthly rather than a true monthly fit.

The brief explicitly distinguishes monthly scoring from a monthly fit. The −1.02 pp figure is the thinned monthly walk-forward minus the quarterly walk-forward, not a true monthly fit scored on quarterly origins. This resolves the earlier ambiguity.

The brief explicitly states that full monthly and quarterly scores are drawn from different origin sets with separate pooled base rates. Skill percentages computed on these distinct bases cannot form a paired loss difference. The −1.02 pp figure therefore cannot be the same-origins diagnostic Fable requested.

The brief lists the −1.02 figure under the code reading of the gate, not as a paired fit comparison. The confidence interval [−4.47, +1.32] is absent from the council brief, so ratifying it would violate the instruction to avoid incorrect information. I am weighing whether this warrants a REJECT with minimal amendments to remove the unverified claim and correct the mislabeling.

I will reject the draft. The false claim in §3.2(b) about the paired same-origins diagnostic is a substantive error that undermines the honest recording of the override. I will propose rewriting that clause to state only the verified thinned score and its difference from the quarterly score, without mislabeling it as the requested paired comparison.

The unverified 10–90 % interval and the false paired-comparison claim are the only remaining blocking issues. Removing them would flip the vote to APPROVE. I am now scanning for any other substantive objections.

The brief’s claim that the curve-only +2.19 has a confidence interval excluding zero is ambiguous. It does not specify whether this refers to the legacy curve-only interval or a separate v5.0.1 interval, and the exact v5.0.1 figure is omitted.

Reason (c) is consistent with the brief. The retroactive exception in §3.4 is explicitly recorded and honest.

The unpaired monthly P is logged unscored, leaving the question open. Declining to apply the preregistered gate is the most post-hoc act in this package, acceptable only because the comparison is unpaired and does not identify a gain.

The brief’s noise range is −1.0 … −3.1 pp for thinned-minus-quarter, and MDE 4.4–8.5. No such CI exists.

I will keep the rejection minimal. §8.3’s pre-2027 EBP fitting clause is not a blocker because my prior veto concerned evidence use, not fitting. I cannot approve with a reservation that §3.2(b) overclaims; ratifying would still record the false sentence.

VOTE: REJECT. The minimal amendment replaces §3.2(b) with the verified thinned score and its −1.02 pp gap, explicitly stating that this is a thinned skill comparison rather than a paired monthly-fit versus quarterly-fit difference.

The minimal amendment now explicitly deletes the false claim that Fable’s paired diagnostic already exists in E2 and removes the unverified interval unless the secretary cites the sealed E2 artifact. It states that the requested monthly-versus-quarterly paired test has not been run, and offers to seal it as an unscored diagnostic before the 2027 refit rather than treating its result as already known.
